newsitem.title: USA: Praxair gets patent on steel making process.
newsitem.headline: Praxair gets patent on steel making process.

text.p: Praxair Inc said Tuesday it had received a U.S. patent for its electric-arc furnace steel-making technology.
The patent covers a process that improves productivity and decreases electrical energy consumption and hazardous emissions in electric arc furnace-based steel mills, Praxair said.

The technology combusts carbon monoxide that is produced during melting and refining to carbon dioxide, Praxair said. The technology allows for an efficent heat transfer during the steel-making process, it said.

Praxair said the process saves 4.5 kilowatt hours for each cubic meter of post-combustion oxygen used in the electric-arc furnace, or as much as a seven to ten percent reduction in electricity consumption.
Praxair has converted seven electric-arc furnaces to its post-combustion technology, representing 3.1 million metric tons of annual production capacity, it said.
By the end of 1996, the company expects to convert two more mills to its process, and another eight mills in 1997.
There are 1,000 steel mills using electric-arc furnaces worldwide, Praxair said.
